== Biography ==
'''Archibald Herbesoun''' was a fisher in Glasgow and the husband of
[[Glasgow-3916|Isobella Glasgow]]. On 27 January 1562/63 the spouses sold a
Bridgegait tenement; the record directly names Archibald's occupation and their
marriage.<ref name="Herbesoun1563">Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 3, protocol 719, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc06scogoog/page/n41/mode/2up p. 29], 27 January 1562/3.</ref>

Archibald was still alive on 19 December 1573, when Robert Glasgow, Archibald
Herbertsone and John Glasgow were collectively described as fishers in a
Bridgegait conveyance. His death is therefore after that date, with no proven
place.<ref name="Herbesoun1573">Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol. 7, protocol 2002, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc00robegoog/page/n52/mode/2up p. 36], 19 December 1573.</ref> A 1575 conveyance refers to a tenement formerly belonging to Archibald Herbertsoun, fisher; that corroborates the property identity but does not prove that he had died.<ref name="Herbesoun1575">Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol. 7, protocol 2151, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc00robegoog/page/n114/mode/2up p. 98], 25 March 1575.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
The 1573 association with Robert and John Glasgow supports a close network
around Isobella, but no record calls either man Archibald's brother-in-law. An
Archibald Herbesoun described as a barker in 1559 and an Archibald Herbertsoun,
baker, in 1574 remain distinct candidates. No parent should be attached until a
record bridges the fisher to an earlier Herbesoun household.

== Biography ==

Isobella Glasgow was married to [[Herbison-475|Archibald Herbisoune]], a fisher. On 27 January 1562/3 the spouses sold a Glasgow tenement on the street leading from the South Port to the bridge over the Clyde. Isobella appeared before a bailie and judicially ratified the transaction.<ref name="Iso1563">Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 3, 1561–1568 (Glasgow, 1897), protocol 719, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc06scogoog/page/n41/mode/2up p. 29], 27 January 1562/3.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

The consolidated Brady/Brade research relevant to this profile is maintained at [[Space:Brady Family of Sauchie, Stirling & Easter Kennet — Research Notes|Brady Family of Stirling and Easter Kennet — Research Notes]].

=== Probable parentage ===

[[Glasgow-1098|William Glasgow]] and [[Brade-232|Isobel Brade]] are probable parents on strong circumstantial evidence, but both relationship links remain uncertain because no act expressly calls Isobella their daughter.

On 28 October 1564 [[Glasgow-1093|John Glesgw]] received sasine as heir of William Glesgw, explicitly his father, in a fore tenement between the lands of the late John Rankin and Robert Young.<ref name="JohnHeir1564">Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol. 3, protocol 805, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc06scogoog/page/n69/mode/2up p. 57], 28 October 1564.</ref> Only nineteen days later John sold that same inherited fore tenement to William Craig. Isobella's husband Archibald Herbisoune witnessed the sale.<ref name="Archibald1564">Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol. 3, protocol 810, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc06scogoog/page/n71/mode/2up pp. 58–59], 16 November 1564.</ref>

This is a direct association between Isobella's proved husband and William's proved son during disposal of paternal inheritance. A close in-law relationship is the simplest explanation, especially because Isobella repeats the forename of proposed mother Isobel Brade and fits the generation. Nevertheless, the witness clause does not call Archibald John's brother-in-law; a trusted neighbour or occupational associate remains possible. The evidence therefore supports ''probable'', not proved, parentage.

The birth date is estimated from Isobella's married property ownership in 1563. She was alive on 27 January 1562/3; that transaction is not a death record.

=== Later Bridgegait evidence ===

On 18 January 1581/2 a neighbouring property's boundaries included the tenement of Archibald Herbertsoun, fisher, on the south side of Bridgegait, with Ninian Schyre's land to the east and the little common green to the south.<ref>Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 8, protocol 2370, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc00scogoog/page/n60/mode/2up pp. 36–37], 18 January 1581/2; Archibald Hegate's protocols, vol. 1, fol. 31.</ref> The name, occupation and street make this a probable later reference to Isobella's husband. It extends the family's property evidence, although the entry does not name Isobella or a Glasgow relative. The particular tenement has not yet been joined to the 1563 title, and this boundary reference supplies no new parentage statement.

public_capture.bio:
{{One Name Study|name=Glasgow}}

== Biography ==

'''Daniel Glasco''' was associated with Lower Norfolk County in the Colony of Virginia during the late seventeenth century. His date and place of birth have not been identified.

The spelling '''Glasco''' is used in the published abstract of the only contemporary record presently identified for him. The original record should be inspected before concluding that this was his consistent surname spelling.

May be a grandson of [[Glasgow-1157|Robert Glasgow II (abt.1612-abt.1690)]]

=== Marriage to Mary Gamon ===

Daniel married '''Mary Gamon''', also rendered Gammon in later accounts, before 4 October 1693.

The will of Mary's father, '''John Gamon''', was dated 4 October 1693 and proved on 15 March 1694. Its published abstract identifies Daniel Glasco as John Gamon's son-in-law and Mary as Daniel's wife. John left Daniel and Mary eighty acres of land bordering Richford Swamp.<ref name="GamonWill">Charles Fleming McIntosh, ''Brief Abstract of Lower Norfolk County and Norfolk County Wills, 1637–1710'' (Virginia: Colonial Dames of America in the State of Virginia, 1914), p. 149, abstract of the will of John Gamon, dated 4 October 1693 and proved 15 March 1694; cited and discussed in Legacy Tree Genealogists, [https://www.legacytree.com/wp-content/uploads/T1508095.CLIENTGlasgow1508.report.public.pdf ''Research Report''] (1 March 2016), p. 3.</ref>

The record directly establishes that:

* Daniel and Mary were married by 4 October 1693;
* Mary's father was John Gamon; and
* Daniel and Mary received land bordering Richford Swamp.

Richford Swamp was situated in Elizabeth River Parish, Lower Norfolk County.<ref name="LegacyReport">Legacy Tree Genealogists, [https://www.legacytree.com/wp-content/uploads/T1508095.CLIENTGlasgow1508.report.public.pdf ''Research Report''] (1 March 2016), pp. 3–4.</ref>

The will abstract does not identify Daniel's parents, birthplace, age, occupation or children.

Daniel was alive on 4 October 1693. His date and place of death have not been identified.

== Research Notes ==

=== Birth date ===

Daniel has previously been assigned a birth year of 1613.

The cited source for that date is an International Genealogical Index entry submitted by an unidentified contributor. The entry contains no supporting source information.<ref name="IGI">The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, “International Genealogical Index (IGI),” database, ''FamilySearch'', [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/2:1:MDL3-HTF entry for Daniel Glasgow] (accessed 4 April 2025); submitted by user jence5408, with no source information supplied.</ref>

A submitted IGI entry records a contributor's assertion. Without an underlying baptism, Bible, will, deed or other historical record, it does not establish that Daniel was born in 1613.

Daniel's birth date and birthplace should therefore be left unknown.

For database purposes, the only certain statement is that he was born before 4 October 1693, when he was recorded as Mary's husband.

=== Unsupported Scottish parentage ===

'''[[Glasgow-1156|Robert Glasgow]]''' and '''[[Ivey-2264|Deborah Ivey]]''' have previously been attached as Daniel's parents.

No inspected record identifies either person as his father or mother.

The will of John Gamon identifies Daniel's wife and father-in-law but does not name Daniel's parents. No Scottish baptism, marriage, testament, land record or migration record has been found connecting Daniel with Robert Glasgow or Deborah Ivey.

Both parental relationships should be removed.

Daniel should also not be attached as a child of '''[[Glasgow-3938|Robert Glasgow]]''', the cordiner who married Jonet or Janet Thomsone in Edinburgh in 1652. No evidence connects that Edinburgh household with Daniel or colonial Virginia.

=== Robert Glasgow and Ann Johnson tradition ===

Many online family trees instead identify Daniel as a son of a Robert Glasgow and Ann Johnson or Johnston.

A professional review of the family found that this relationship was repeated in online trees but that those trees supplied no documentary evidence supporting it.<ref name="LegacyReport" />

No contemporary record presently establishes that:

* Robert Glasgow and Ann Johnson were Daniel's parents;
* Daniel was born in Scotland;
* Daniel migrated from Scotland to Virginia; or
* Daniel belonged to the Scottish Glasgow families represented by the earlier profiles.

Any attachment to Robert Glasgow and Ann Johnson should remain uncertain or be removed until a contemporary parentage record is found.

=== Possible connection with Robert Glascocke ===

A Robert Glascocke was documented in the Elizabeth River area before Daniel's known appearance there.

Robert Glascocke received:

* a patent for 200 acres in Elizabeth City County on 7 October 1635; and
* a patent for another fifty acres in Lower New Norfolk County on 10 June 1639.

A 1640 court order also referred to religious services being held at Robert Glascocke's house while a meetinghouse was being built.<ref name="LegacyReport" />

The shared locality and broadly similar surnames make Robert Glascocke a person worth investigating as a possible relative.

They do not prove that:

* Robert Glascocke was Daniel's father;
* Glascocke and Glasco were forms used by the same family;
* Robert married Ann Johnson;
* Daniel inherited Robert's land; or
* either man belonged to a Scottish Glasgow family.

Robert Glascocke should not be attached as Daniel's father without a deed, will, court record or other document connecting them.

=== Surname ===

The published abstract of John Gamon's will records Daniel's surname as '''Glasco'''.

Later records and compiled genealogies use variants including:

* Glasco;
* Glasgow;
* Glascock;
* Glasscock; and
* Glascocke.

Surname spelling was not fully standardised during this period, but similarity alone does not prove that all these records concern one family.

The original will should be inspected to establish the spelling used by the clerk. Until then, Glasco is the best-supported spelling for Daniel himself, with Glasgow retained as an alternate form where appropriate.

=== Children ===

No inspected contemporary record identifies a child of Daniel Glasco and Mary Gamon.

Later family trees attribute children and extensive descendants to the couple, but those relationships should not be treated as established solely because they appear in compiled genealogies.

Each proposed child requires separate evidence, such as:

* a baptism or parish entry;
* a deed describing the relationship;
* a will naming the child;
* a guardianship record;
* an apprenticeship record;
* a court order; or
* a documented chain of inherited land.

Any existing child attachments should remain uncertain pending review of their individual evidence.

=== The inherited property ===

John Gamon's will left Daniel and Mary eighty acres bordering Richford Swamp.

Tracing that property may be the best route for identifying Daniel's later life and possible children. Deeds involving its later sale, inheritance or division may name Daniel's heirs or establish whether he had died.

The original will, probate proceedings and subsequent land records should be obtained rather than relying solely on the published abstract.

=== Death ===

Daniel's date and place of death are unknown.

He was alive when John Gamon's will was written on 4 October 1693. The will's probate on 15 March 1694 does not necessarily prove Daniel was still living on that later date.

His death should therefore be recorded as after 4 October 1693 only if an estimated date is required. No precise death place should be assigned.

=== Further research ===

Useful remaining records include:

* the original will of John Gamon;
* the complete probate file and estate accounts;
* deeds concerning the eighty acres bordering Richford Swamp;
* Lower Norfolk County court orders;
* Elizabeth River Parish records;
* later Norfolk and Princess Anne County deeds and probate records;
* records identifying Daniel and Mary's children or heirs;
* land records concerning Robert Glascocke's patents;
* evidence establishing whether Glasco, Glasgow and Glascocke were used for the same family;
* contemporary records concerning Ann Johnson or Johnston;
* any immigration or transportation record for Daniel;
* a will or estate administration for Daniel;
* a will or estate administration for Mary; and
* the original evidence underlying the submitted IGI entry.

== Biography ==
Hugh is currently estimated to have been born about 1600 and is associated with Ayrshire. Both the estimate and the geographic association derive from the cited online tree and remain uncertain.

== Research Notes ==
No reviewed record yet proves Hugh's identity, birth, father, or son. The existing links to [[Glasgow-991|James Glasgow]] as father and [[Glasgow-1604|John Glasgow]] as son are retained as '''uncertain scaffold relationships'''.

James Glasgow's documented household is centred on Calder and Inveresk in Midlothian, while this profile's working hypothesis is Ayrshire; that geographic mismatch makes the present father attachment especially tentative. A more plausible broad route may lie in the Corsankell–Stevenston–Kilwinning cluster beneath [[Glasgow-1098|William Glasgow]], but no source identifies Hugh's exact place in it.

A 1571 record names James elder of Corsankell and his sons James and John, but does not name Hugh.<ref>National Records of Scotland, [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/details.aspx?reference=GD39%2F5%2F59 GD39/5/59], 1571.</ref> The Glasgow commissary testament index also identifies John at Montfoid (1610), James at Brekpleughe (1632), and Ninian at Brigend of Eglinton (1634).<ref>Francis J. Grant, ed., [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso07scotuoft ''Commissariot Record of Glasgow: Register of Testaments, 1547–1800''], surname index.</ref> These records establish nearby candidate households and may indicate a missing generation or conflated placeholder; they do not prove Hugh. He could be a son or grandson of [[Glasgow-3193|John Glasgow]], but no direct attachment should be made without a record.

A 1677 printed Register of Deeds index lists “Hugh, preacher of the gospel” under Glasgow. The same row calls him grantee (“Ge.”) in a deed indexed as “Transl.”, recorded 8 March 1677 at the Durie Office, volume 42, page 148 (NRS RD3/42, p. 148). This is a possible match only: the index gives no locality or relatives, and it does not identify the man with this profile. 8 March is the date the deed was recorded, not a death date. The underlying deed must be examined before changing this profile's dates or family links.<ref>FamilySearch, ''Scotland. Land Records 1677'', item #007830797, Item 3, image 48; printed ''Register of Deeds, 1677. Name and Designation'', vol. XVII, p. 80, s.v. [[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==

'''James Glasgow'''—also recorded as '''James Glasco'''—was a mariner and shipmaster associated with Belfast, County Antrim, during the later seventeenth century. His origins, parentage, date of birth, wife, and children have not been identified.

The available evidence places James in Belfast’s maritime community from at least 1667 until 1679. Although an estimated birth around 1600 has sometimes been assigned to him, no contemporary record supporting that date has been found. He was necessarily born before 1667 and was probably an adult by then.

On 29 October 1667, Belfast merchant George Macartney reported that Mr Arthur wished to ship butter from Belfast to Rouen but had been unable to obtain a vessel. Macartney therefore proposed sending the butter to Dublin aboard the ''Blessing'' of Saltcoats, of which James Glasgow was master.<ref>Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, MIC19/2, business correspondence of George Macartney, letter dated 29 October 1667.</ref> This record identifies James as the master of a Scottish vessel engaged in trade between Belfast and Dublin, with the cargo intended ultimately for France.

On 21 January 1669/70, James was admitted and sworn as a free commoner of the Corporation of Belfast. The entry records him as:

: “James Glasco Marriner Admitted and sworne a ffree Comoner”

A fee of ten shillings was entered beside his name.<ref>Robert Magill Young, ed., ''The Town Book of the Corporation of Belfast, 1613–1816'' (Belfast: Marcus Ward & Co., 1892), p. 271; entry dated 21 January 1669 [Old Style, equivalent to 21 January 1670 New Style].</ref>

Admission as a free commoner gave James formal standing within the borough. The record is also direct contemporary evidence of his occupation and presence in Belfast.

James continued to work as a shipmaster during the following decade. On 8 November 1679, George Macartney recorded that he had freighted the ''James of Belfast'', commanded by James Glasgow, to carry butter and tallow to Havre de Grâce, now Le Havre, France.<ref>Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, MIC19/2, business correspondence of George Macartney, letter dated 8 November 1679.</ref> Macartney referred to the arrangement again that day in correspondence with Sir Joshua Allen concerning the payment of bills.<ref>Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, MIC19/2, business correspondence of George Macartney, letter from George Macartney to Sir Joshua Allen, dated 8 November 1679.</ref>

These records show James commanding at least two vessels—the ''Blessing'' of Saltcoats in 1667 and the ''James of Belfast'' in 1679—and participating in trade linking Belfast with Dublin and French ports. The surviving evidence supports describing him as a mariner and shipmaster. It does not establish that he owned either vessel or that he held the title of captain in a military or naval sense.

A testamentary reference for a James Glasgow of Belfast carries the year 1686 in the Connor will material.<ref>Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, T/828/15, Connor Will Extracts and pre-1858 wills index, entry for James Glasgow of Belfast, 1686.</ref> The original will has not been examined, and its contents are presently unknown. The close agreement of name, place, occupation period, and date makes it probable that the testamentary record relates to the mariner, but this identification should remain qualified until the extract or surviving copy is consulted.

The year 1686 has not been established as his death or probate date: it may be the date of the will. His last dated lifetime record presently cited is the letter of 8 November 1679, so the death field is conservatively recorded as after that date. His place of death is also unproved. No reliable evidence has yet been found identifying his wife, children, parents, or descendants.

== Research Notes ==

* The surname appears as both ''Glasgow'' and ''Glasco''.
* The Corporation record uses Old Style dating. Its “21 January 1669” corresponds to 21 January 1670 under the modern calendar because the legal year then began on 25 March.
* A birth around 1600 is not supported by the cited records. It would make James about sixty-seven when first recorded as a working shipmaster and about seventy-nine in 1679. This is possible but presently speculative.
* Belfast should be treated as James’s place of residence or occupational association, not as a proved birthplace.
* The 1686 will-index entry is probably his, but the identification is not conclusive without examining the will extract.
* No evidence currently supports the claim that he left descendants or property in Belfast.

=== Possible north-east Antrim placement ===
Captain James is a possible son or younger relative of [[Glasgow-3970|Robert Glaskow of Larne]] and a possible collateral of the adjacent Kilwaughter householders [[Glasgow-3913|John Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-1081|James Glascho]]. Belfast, Larne and Kilwaughter form a credible north-east Antrim maritime and estate corridor, and a shipmaster active by 1667 fits the generation after Robert's 1653 occurrence. The evidence is geographical and chronological only; no record states a relationship.<ref>Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, MIC19/2, maritime material naming Captain James Glasgow or Glascow as a Belfast-associated shipmaster in the late 1660s and 1670s.</ref>

Captain James and the Kilwaughter James represented by [[Glasgow-1081]] are retained as separate, unproved identities. A will dated 1686 does not alone exclude survival to the 1720s. Conversely, the identification of the 1669 Kilwaughter householder with the later congregational officer is itself a continuity inference; an adult householder in 1669 surviving to 1726 would be at least about 78, and a same-name successor must be considered. The complete Belfast will extract and the Kilwaughter records are needed to decide this question.<ref>Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, T/828/15, will extract for James Glasgow of Belfast, 1686.</ref>

== Sources ==

<references />

* Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, MIC19/2, business correspondence of George Macartney, merchant, 1672–1681, including related earlier material.
* Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, T/828/15, Connor Will Extracts and pre-1858 wills index.
* Young, Robert Magill, ed. ''The Town Book of the Corporation of Belfast, 1613–1816''. Belfast: Marcus Ward & Co., 1892, p. 271.

maintained_current_conclusions:
PRONI references support a Belfast-associated shipmaster active from at least
1667 and a Belfast will in 1686. The profile's birth about 1600 is unsupported.
He is a genuine Belfast maritime root witness, but no reviewed source identifies
him with the Kilwaughter James or supplies parents or children.

== Biography ==

James Glasgow was recorded at Glasgow on 25 November 1645 as the son of Robert Glasgow and Jonet Cunynghame. The register names James Cunynghame and Johne Muir as godfathers.<ref name="SP1645">Scotland's People, Church of Scotland Old Parish Registers, births and baptisms, Glasgow parish 644/1, reference 40/56, James Glasgow, male, 25 November 1645, parents indexed as "Rot. Glasgow/Jonet Cunnyngham". Original register image inspected 31 August 2026; it names James Cunynghame and Johne Muir as godfathers but gives no occupation, residence, age or birthplace for Robert.</ref>

The attached father, [[Glasgow-1078|Robert Glasgow]], baptised at Glasgow in 1618, is chronologically compatible but is not identified by the index. That relationship remains uncertain. The attached mother, [[Cunningham-22604|Jonet Cunningham]], represents the woman named in the 1645 record.

This Scottish child has been proposed as identical with [[Glasgow-1081|James Glasgow of Kilwaughter]], County Antrim, first securely recorded there in 1669. No inspected record supplies migration, residence, occupation or family evidence joining them, so they must remain separate profiles.

== Research Notes ==

=== Godfather identification ===

The obvious James Cunningham, merchant and burgess admitted in 1629, had a testament confirmed on 31 January 1642 and therefore cannot have been the living godfather in 1645. Other men of the name—including James Cunningham of Easter Garden and later burgess entrants associated with Dunoon and Cobblehaugh—remain possible, but none has been connected to this baptism.<ref name="Indexes">James R. Anderson, ed., [https://www.electricscotland.com/history/records/scottishrecordso43scotuoft.pdf ''Burgesses & Guild Brethren of Glasgow, 1573–1750'']; Scottish Record Society, [https://archive.org/stream/scottishrecordso07scotuoft/scottishrecordso07scotuoft_djvu.txt ''The Commissariot Record of Glasgow: Register of Testaments, 1547–1800''], surname entries for Cunningham and Muir.</ref>

The same-name problem is greater for Johne Muir. The testament index excludes a Glasgow tailor whose testament was confirmed in 1640 and a mariner whose testament was confirmed in 1642. Men described in later entries as a maltman, weaver, doctor and of Langside could have been alive in 1645. An early John Muir in the cordiner membership material dates from 1585 and cannot be selected merely because James's possible grandfather was a cordiner. Both godfathers therefore remain unidentified.

== Sources ==

* "Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQHK-VMK), James Glasgow, 1645. Derivative index to the same event.

public_capture.Name: Glasgow-3107
public_capture.bio:
== Biography == 

'''James Glasgow''' married '''Agnes Watt''' (recorded as Agnes Waitt or Waitte) on 18 June 1663 in Polwarth, Berwickshire, Scotland.<ref name="marriageRecordScotlandsPeople">“James Glasgow and Agnes Waitte,” Old Parish Registers - Banns and Marriages, National Records of Scotland (ScotlandsPeople), Parish Number 754, Ref 10/62, Frame 37, Polwarth, Berwickshire; marriage date 18 June 1663.</ref><ref name="marriageRecordFS">"Scotland, Marriages, 1561-1910", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTL8-X6D : 11 February 2020), James Glasgow, marriage to Agnes Waitte, 18 Jun 1663, Polwarth, Berwickshire, Scotland.</ref> His parentage remains unconfirmed. While some online trees suggest a birth year around 1640,<ref>See, for example, the FamilySearch profile GKWN-35S which associates this marriage with a 1640 birth year, though this profile demonstrably conflates individuals (see Possible Confusions section).</ref> this is an estimate likely based on his marriage date; he was probably born in the early-to-mid 17th century.

Polwarth is a parish located in the historic county of Berwickshire, near the town of Duns. Following their marriage, James and Agnes appear to have settled in the adjacent parish of Gordon, Berwickshire. A series of baptism records in Gordon list a James Glasgow (or Glascow) as the father of several children between 1666 and 1679. Given the proximity of Gordon to Polwarth, the consistent father's name, and the timing relative to the 1663 marriage, these children are very likely the issue of James and Agnes Watt:
*   '''[[Glasgow-3117|John Glasgow (1666-)]]''', christened 29 April 1666.<ref name="johnBaptismFS">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTBS-Z9H : 16 September 2021), James Glascow in entry for John Glascow, christened 29 Apr 1666, Gordon, Berwickshire, Scotland.</ref>
*   '''[[Glasgow-1440|Patrick Glasgow (abt.1667-)]]''', christened 4 August 1667.<ref name="patrickBaptismFS">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTBS-98Z : 16 September 2021), James Glasgow in entry for Patrike Glasgow, christened 4 Aug 1667, Gordon, Berwickshire, Scotland.</ref>
*   '''[[Glasgow-3364|Jean Glasgow (1671-)]]''', christened 16 April 1671.<ref name="jeanBaptismFS">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYLM-Y4Z : 16 September 2021), James Glasgow in entry for Jean Glasgow, christened 16 Apr 1671, Gordon, Berwickshire, Scotland.</ref>
*   '''[[Glasgow-3106|Robert Glasgow (1673-)]]''', christened 1 April 1673.<ref name="robertBaptismFS">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYHJ-3R9 : 16 September 2021), James Glasgow in entry for Robert Glasgow, christened 1 Apr 1673, Gordon, Berwickshire, Scotland.</ref>
*   '''[[Glasgow-3363|Agnes Glasgow (1676-)]]''', christened 29 October 1676.<ref name="agnesBaptismFS">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYLM-Y4H : 16 September 2021), James Glasgow in entry for Agnes Glasgow, christened 29 Oct 1676, Gordon, Berwickshire, Scotland.</ref>
*   '''[[Glasgow-3365|Margaret Glasgow (1679-)]]''', christened 24 May 1679.<ref name="margratBaptismFS">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYL9-Q32 : 16 September 2021), James Glasgow in entry for Margrat Glasgow, christened 24 May 1679, Gordon, Berwickshire, Scotland.</ref>

The christening of a daughter named Agnes in 1676 strongly supports the identification of this family unit with the 1663 marriage of James Glasgow and Agnes Watt, following common naming patterns. While the indexed baptism records from FamilySearch do not include the mother's name, the circumstantial evidence linking these Gordon children to James and Agnes (Watt) of Polwarth is compelling.

Further evidence of the family's presence in Gordon comes from the marriage record of their daughter, Jean. On 3 June 1702, '''John Smith''' married '''Jean Glasgow''' in Gordon, Berwickshire. The record explicitly names the bride's father as '''James Glasgow'''.<ref name="jeanMarriageFS">"Scotland, Marriages, 1561-1910", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTLH-1MB : 11 February 2020), James Glasgow in entry for John Smith and Jean Glasgow, 3 Jun 1702, Gordon, Berwickshire, Scotland.</ref> This confirms Jean survived to adulthood and indicates the family's continued connection to the Gordon parish into the early 18th century. The record identifies James as Jean's father but does not necessarily confirm he was still living in 1702.

Beyond these records, specific details about James's occupation or death date remain unconfirmed in contemporary Scottish sources.

== Research Notes ==

Likely a relative of the father of a William Glasgow, father of [[Glasgow-1605|William Glasgow (bef.1658-)]] in Polworth, Berwickshire. These are the first two Glasgow's to appear in this area. (brothers?) 

=== Possible Confusions with Ulster Glasgows ===
Genealogical research on this James Glasgow is complicated by the presence of other men with the same name in 17th-century records, particularly in Ulster, Ireland. Several online genealogies and collaborative trees (such as FamilySearch profile GKWN-35S, which attaches the Polwarth marriage, the Gordon baptisms, ''and'' a 1725 death date) have mistakenly connected James Glasgow of Polwarth and Gordon to the James Glasgow who settled in Kilwaughter Parish, County Antrim, Ireland. This Kilwaughter James appears in the 1669 Hearth Money Rolls for County Antrim and reportedly died in 1726.<ref name="kilwaughterInfo">This information regarding the Kilwaughter James is commonly cited in Glasgow family histories but requires primary source verification for the death date and details. Secondary sources often cite a James Glasgow in Kilwaughter, Co. Antrim, appearing in the 1669 Hearth Money Rolls and dying c. 1726. Primary source verification is recommended. public_capture.Name: Glasgow-3172
public_capture.bio:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==

'''James Glasgow'''—also recorded as '''James Glasco'''—was a mariner and shipmaster associated with Belfast, County Antrim, during the later seventeenth century. His origins, parentage, date of birth, wife, and children have not been identified.

The available evidence places James in Belfast’s maritime community from at least 1667 until 1679. Although an estimated birth around 1600 has sometimes been assigned to him, no contemporary record supporting that date has been found. He was necessarily born before 1667 and was probably an adult by then.

On 29 October 1667, Belfast merchant George Macartney reported that Mr Arthur wished to ship butter from Belfast to Rouen but had been unable to obtain a vessel. Macartney therefore proposed sending the butter to Dublin aboard the ''Blessing'' of Saltcoats, of which James Glasgow was master.<ref>Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, MIC19/2, business correspondence of George Macartney, letter dated 29 October 1667.</ref> This record identifies James as the master of a Scottish vessel engaged in trade between Belfast and Dublin, with the cargo intended ultimately for France.

On 21 January 1669/70, James was admitted and sworn as a free commoner of the Corporation of Belfast. The entry records him as:

: “James Glasco Marriner Admitted and sworne a ffree Comoner”

A fee of ten shillings was entered beside his name.<ref>Robert Magill Young, ed., ''The Town Book of the Corporation of Belfast, 1613–1816'' (Belfast: Marcus Ward & Co., 1892), p. 271; entry dated 21 January 1669 [Old Style, equivalent to 21 January 1670 New Style].</ref>

Admission as a free commoner gave James formal standing within the borough. The record is also direct contemporary evidence of his occupation and presence in Belfast.

James continued to work as a shipmaster during the following decade. On 8 November 1679, George Macartney recorded that he had freighted the ''James of Belfast'', commanded by James Glasgow, to carry butter and tallow to Havre de Grâce, now Le Havre, France.<ref>Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, MIC19/2, business correspondence of George Macartney, letter dated 8 November 1679.</ref> Macartney referred to the arrangement again that day in correspondence with Sir Joshua Allen concerning the payment of bills.<ref>Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, MIC19/2, business correspondence of George Macartney, letter from George Macartney to Sir Joshua Allen, dated 8 November 1679.</ref>

These records show James commanding at least two vessels—the ''Blessing'' of Saltcoats in 1667 and the ''James of Belfast'' in 1679—and participating in trade linking Belfast with Dublin and French ports. The surviving evidence supports describing him as a mariner and shipmaster. It does not establish that he owned either vessel or that he held the title of captain in a military or naval sense.

A testamentary reference for a James Glasgow of Belfast carries the year 1686 in the Connor will material.<ref>Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, T/828/15, Connor Will Extracts and pre-1858 wills index, entry for James Glasgow of Belfast, 1686.</ref> The original will has not been examined, and its contents are presently unknown. The close agreement of name, place, occupation period, and date makes it probable that the testamentary record relates to the mariner, but this identification should remain qualified until the extract or surviving copy is consulted.

The year 1686 has not been established as his death or probate date: it may be the date of the will. His last dated lifetime record presently cited is the letter of 8 November 1679, so the death field is conservatively recorded as after that date. His place of death is also unproved. No reliable evidence has yet been found identifying his wife, children, parents, or descendants.

== Research Notes ==

* The surname appears as both ''Glasgow'' and ''Glasco''.
* The Corporation record uses Old Style dating. Its “21 January 1669” corresponds to 21 January 1670 under the modern calendar because the legal year then began on 25 March.
* A birth around 1600 is not supported by the cited records. It would make James about sixty-seven when first recorded as a working shipmaster and about seventy-nine in 1679. This is possible but presently speculative.
* Belfast should be treated as James’s place of residence or occupational association, not as a proved birthplace.
* The 1686 will-index entry is probably his, but the identification is not conclusive without examining the will extract.
* No evidence currently supports the claim that he left descendants or property in Belfast.

=== Possible north-east Antrim placement ===
Captain James is a possible son or younger relative of [[Glasgow-3970|Robert Glaskow of Larne]] and a possible collateral of the adjacent Kilwaughter householders [[Glasgow-3913|John Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-1081|James Glascho]]. Belfast, Larne and Kilwaughter form a credible north-east Antrim maritime and estate corridor, and a shipmaster active by 1667 fits the generation after Robert's 1653 occurrence. The evidence is geographical and chronological only; no record states a relationship.<ref>Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, MIC19/2, maritime material naming Captain James Glasgow or Glascow as a Belfast-associated shipmaster in the late 1660s and 1670s.</ref>

Captain James and the Kilwaughter James represented by [[Glasgow-1081]] are retained as separate, unproved identities. A will dated 1686 does not alone exclude survival to the 1720s. Conversely, the identification of the 1669 Kilwaughter householder with the later congregational officer is itself a continuity inference; an adult householder in 1669 surviving to 1726 would be at least about 78, and a same-name successor must be considered. The complete Belfast will extract and the Kilwaughter records are needed to decide this question.<ref>Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, T/828/15, will extract for James Glasgow of Belfast, 1686.</ref>

== Sources ==

<references />

* Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, MIC19/2, business correspondence of George Macartney, merchant, 1672–1681, including related earlier material.
* Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, T/828/15, Connor Will Extracts and pre-1858 wills index.
* Young, Robert Magill, ed. ''The Town Book of the Corporation of Belfast, 1613–1816''. Belfast: Marcus Ward & Co., 1892, p. 271.

== Biography ==

James Glasgow was recorded at Glasgow on 25 November 1645 as the son of Robert Glasgow and Jonet Cunynghame. The register names James Cunynghame and Johne Muir as godfathers.<ref name="SP1645">Scotland's People, Church of Scotland Old Parish Registers, births and baptisms, Glasgow parish 644/1, reference 40/56, James Glasgow, male, 25 November 1645, parents indexed as "Rot. Glasgow/Jonet Cunnyngham". Original register image inspected 31 August 2026; it names James Cunynghame and Johne Muir as godfathers but gives no occupation, residence, age or birthplace for Robert.</ref>

The attached father, [[Glasgow-1078|Robert Glasgow]], baptised at Glasgow in 1618, is chronologically compatible but is not identified by the index. That relationship remains uncertain. The attached mother, [[Cunningham-22604|Jonet Cunningham]], represents the woman named in the 1645 record.

This Scottish child has been proposed as identical with [[Glasgow-1081|James Glasgow of Kilwaughter]], County Antrim, first securely recorded there in 1669. No inspected record supplies migration, residence, occupation or family evidence joining them, so they must remain separate profiles.

== Research Notes ==

=== Godfather identification ===

The obvious James Cunningham, merchant and burgess admitted in 1629, had a testament confirmed on 31 January 1642 and therefore cannot have been the living godfather in 1645. Other men of the name—including James Cunningham of Easter Garden and later burgess entrants associated with Dunoon and Cobblehaugh—remain possible, but none has been connected to this baptism.<ref name="Indexes">James R. Anderson, ed., [https://www.electricscotland.com/history/records/scottishrecordso43scotuoft.pdf ''Burgesses & Guild Brethren of Glasgow, 1573–1750'']; Scottish Record Society, [https://archive.org/stream/scottishrecordso07scotuoft/scottishrecordso07scotuoft_djvu.txt ''The Commissariot Record of Glasgow: Register of Testaments, 1547–1800''], surname entries for Cunningham and Muir.</ref>

The same-name problem is greater for Johne Muir. The testament index excludes a Glasgow tailor whose testament was confirmed in 1640 and a mariner whose testament was confirmed in 1642. Men described in later entries as a maltman, weaver, doctor and of Langside could have been alive in 1645. An early John Muir in the cordiner membership material dates from 1585 and cannot be selected merely because James's possible grandfather was a cordiner. Both godfathers therefore remain unidentified.

* "Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQHK-VMK), James Glasgow, 1645. Derivative index to the same event.

== Biography == 

'''James Glasgow''' married '''Agnes Watt''' (recorded as Agnes Waitt or Waitte) on 18 June 1663 in Polwarth, Berwickshire, Scotland.<ref name="marriageRecordScotlandsPeople">“James Glasgow and Agnes Waitte,” Old Parish Registers - Banns and Marriages, National Records of Scotland (ScotlandsPeople), Parish Number 754, Ref 10/62, Frame 37, Polwarth, Berwickshire; marriage date 18 June 1663.</ref><ref name="marriageRecordFS">"Scotland, Marriages, 1561-1910", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTL8-X6D : 11 February 2020), James Glasgow, marriage to Agnes Waitte, 18 Jun 1663, Polwarth, Berwickshire, Scotland.</ref> His parentage remains unconfirmed. While some online trees suggest a birth year around 1640,<ref>See, for example, the FamilySearch profile GKWN-35S which associates this marriage with a 1640 birth year, though this profile demonstrably conflates individuals (see Possible Confusions section).</ref> this is an estimate likely based on his marriage date; he was probably born in the early-to-mid 17th century.

Polwarth is a parish located in the historic county of Berwickshire, near the town of Duns. Following their marriage, James and Agnes appear to have settled in the adjacent parish of Gordon, Berwickshire. A series of baptism records in Gordon list a James Glasgow (or Glascow) as the father of several children between 1666 and 1679. Given the proximity of Gordon to Polwarth, the consistent father's name, and the timing relative to the 1663 marriage, these children are very likely the issue of James and Agnes Watt:
*   '''[[Glasgow-3117|John Glasgow (1666-)]]''', christened 29 April 1666.<ref name="johnBaptismFS">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTBS-Z9H : 16 September 2021), James Glascow in entry for John Glascow, christened 29 Apr 1666, Gordon, Berwickshire, Scotland.</ref>
*   '''[[Glasgow-1440|Patrick Glasgow (abt.1667-)]]''', christened 4 August 1667.<ref name="patrickBaptismFS">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTBS-98Z : 16 September 2021), James Glasgow in entry for Patrike Glasgow, christened 4 Aug 1667, Gordon, Berwickshire, Scotland.</ref>
*   '''[[Glasgow-3364|Jean Glasgow (1671-)]]''', christened 16 April 1671.<ref name="jeanBaptismFS">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYLM-Y4Z : 16 September 2021), James Glasgow in entry for Jean Glasgow, christened 16 Apr 1671, Gordon, Berwickshire, Scotland.</ref>
*   '''[[Glasgow-3106|Robert Glasgow (1673-)]]''', christened 1 April 1673.<ref name="robertBaptismFS">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYHJ-3R9 : 16 September 2021), James Glasgow in entry for Robert Glasgow, christened 1 Apr 1673, Gordon, Berwickshire, Scotland.</ref>
*   '''[[Glasgow-3363|Agnes Glasgow (1676-)]]''', christened 29 October 1676.<ref name="agnesBaptismFS">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYLM-Y4H : 16 September 2021), James Glasgow in entry for Agnes Glasgow, christened 29 Oct 1676, Gordon, Berwickshire, Scotland.</ref>
*   '''[[Glasgow-3365|Margaret Glasgow (1679-)]]''', christened 24 May 1679.<ref name="margratBaptismFS">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYL9-Q32 : 16 September 2021), James Glasgow in entry for Margrat Glasgow, christened 24 May 1679, Gordon, Berwickshire, Scotland.</ref>

The christening of a daughter named Agnes in 1676 strongly supports the identification of this family unit with the 1663 marriage of James Glasgow and Agnes Watt, following common naming patterns. While the indexed baptism records from FamilySearch do not include the mother's name, the circumstantial evidence linking these Gordon children to James and Agnes (Watt) of Polwarth is compelling.

Further evidence of the family's presence in Gordon comes from the marriage record of their daughter, Jean. On 3 June 1702, '''John Smith''' married '''Jean Glasgow''' in Gordon, Berwickshire. The record explicitly names the bride's father as '''James Glasgow'''.<ref name="jeanMarriageFS">"Scotland, Marriages, 1561-1910", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTLH-1MB : 11 February 2020), James Glasgow in entry for John Smith and Jean Glasgow, 3 Jun 1702, Gordon, Berwickshire, Scotland.</ref> This confirms Jean survived to adulthood and indicates the family's continued connection to the Gordon parish into the early 18th century. The record identifies James as Jean's father but does not necessarily confirm he was still living in 1702.

Beyond these records, specific details about James's occupation or death date remain unconfirmed in contemporary Scottish sources.

== Research Notes ==

Likely a relative of the father of a William Glasgow, father of [[Glasgow-1605|William Glasgow (bef.1658-)]] in Polworth, Berwickshire. These are the first two Glasgow's to appear in this area. (brothers?) 

=== Possible Confusions with Ulster Glasgows ===
Genealogical research on this James Glasgow is complicated by the presence of other men with the same name in 17th-century records, particularly in Ulster, Ireland. Several online genealogies and collaborative trees (such as FamilySearch profile GKWN-35S, which attaches the Polwarth marriage, the Gordon baptisms, ''and'' a 1725 death date) have mistakenly connected James Glasgow of Polwarth and Gordon to the James Glasgow who settled in Kilwaughter Parish, County Antrim, Ireland. This Kilwaughter James appears in the 1669 Hearth Money Rolls for County Antrim and reportedly died in 1726.<ref name="kilwaughterInfo">This information regarding the Kilwaughter James is commonly cited in Glasgow family histories but requires primary source verification for the death date and details. Secondary sources often cite a James Glasgow in Kilwaughter, Co. Antrim, appearing in the 1669 Hearth Money Rolls and dying c. 1726. Primary source verification is recommended. This individual is considered distinct from James Glasgow of Polwarth/Gordon.</ref>

Crucially, there is currently no known documentary evidence directly linking the James Glasgow who married Agnes Watt in Polwarth (1663) and raised a family in Gordon, Berwickshire (c. 1666-1679+), to the James Glasgow recorded in Kilwaughter, County Antrim. The established family life in Berwickshire during the period the Kilwaughter James was documented in Ireland strongly suggests these were two distinct individuals. Researchers should treat them separately. The 1725/1726 death date often associated with James Glasgow belongs to the Kilwaughter individual, not the James of Polwarth and Gordon.

== Biography ==

'''John Glasgow''' is estimated to have been born about 1813 in Ireland. An unsourced family tree handed down to [[Glasgow-933|M Glasgow]] identifies him as the husband of Elizabeth Fee and places their marriage before 1845 in Ireland.<ref name="FamilyTree">Unsourced family tree handed down to [[Glasgow-933|M Glasgow]].</ref> Those details remain a family reconstruction rather than a proved identification.

== Research Notes ==

=== Parentage and identity ===

The 1851 census of [[Glasgow-1367|Robert Glasgow]]'s Glenleslie household records his son John, aged forty, a labourer, absent in '''America'''.<ref name="Glenleslie1851">[https://durrushistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/10/1851irishcensusreturnscommadelimitedtextfilejul24_071.pdf ''1851 Irish Census Returns: detailed comma-delimited transcription''], Glenleslie household 23.</ref> That census-identified man now has the separate profile [[Glasgow-4055|John Glasgow]]. This profile is retained for the County Armagh family attached through Elizabeth Fee and Samuel; no record links that family to Robert's absent son.

Robert's son was not the same person as the forty-year-old nephew living with [[Glasgow-1022|John Glasgow]] in nearby household 21. The nephew was resident at Glenleslie, worked as a linen weaver and reported a first marriage in 1839.<ref name="Glenleslie1851" />

=== County Armagh family ===

The family attached through Elizabeth Fee and their reported son Samuel points instead toward County Armagh. A published biography of Samuel's son states that Samuel came from Armagh to Queensland in 1863.<ref name="SenateBio">[https://biography.senate.gov.au/glasgow-thomas-william/ Biographical Dictionary of the Australian Senate], Thomas William Glasgow.</ref>

A separate John Glasgow, widowed farmer, died at Killyreavy, County Armagh, on 27 December 1882 aged 66. His son-in-law James Campbell reported the death.<ref name="KillyreavyDeath">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1883/06378/4830400.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil death register], John Glasgow, Killyreavy, 27 December 1882.</ref> Campbell had married Martha Jane Glasgow, daughter of John Glasgow, farmer of Killyreavy, on 20 February 1873.<ref name="CampbellMarriage">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1873/11258/8128996.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register], James Campbell and Martha Jane Glasgow, First Keady Presbyterian Church, 20 February 1873.</ref> These records establish a distinct Armagh John and daughter, but do not yet prove that he was Elizabeth Fee's husband or Samuel's father.

The exact identity of the County Armagh John remains unresolved. He should not be merged with [[Glasgow-4055|Robert's census-identified son]] unless a record explicitly connects the two families.
* Candidate death entry: John Glasgow, 30 September 1871, aged 56, Omagh district, D/1871/209/1025/2/489. [https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/death GRONI death index].
* Candidate death entry: John Glasgow, 11 December 1882, aged 66, Armagh district, D/1883/11/1002/12/140. [https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/death GRONI death index].

== Sources ==

== Biography ==

John Glasgow was a brother of [[Glasgow-3188|Ninian Glasgow]] and is identified as a son of [[Glasgow-1096|Robert Glasgow]], a fisher and burgess of Glasgow.<ref name="Ninian">James R. Anderson, ed., ''Burgesses & Guild Brethren of Glasgow, 1573-1750'' (Scottish Record Society, 1925), [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso43scotuoft/page/24/mode/2up p. 24], entry dated 23 October 1596: “Glasgow, Ninian, B. and F., as second son to Robert G., fisher, burgess”; National Records of Scotland, Glasgow Commissary Court, CC9/7/9, images 142–145, testament testamentar and inventory of Ninian Glasgow, made 10 January 1613 and confirmed 8 May 1613: “Item to Johne glasgw his brother ane new gowne.”</ref> His date and place of birth are unknown, and his mother has not been identified.

John was living on 10 January 1613, when Ninian made his testament at Glasgow and left him a new gown.<ref name="Ninian" />

He was probably the John Glasgow who married [[Mathie-159|Jonet Mathie]], recorded as Jonat Mathen, at Glasgow on 25 January 1618.<ref name="Marriage1618">“Scotland, Marriages, 1561-1910”, database, ''FamilySearch'' (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYWK-WMQ : 11 February 2020), Johne Glasgow, 1618.</ref> That couple had the following children baptised in the High Church of Glasgow:

* [[Glasgow-1088|John Glasgow]], baptised 13 May 1619.<ref name="John1619">“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950”, database, ''FamilySearch'' (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQHV-12T : 16 September 2021), Johne Glasgow in entry for Johne Glasgow, 1619. Mother recorded as Jonat Mathei.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-1089|Jonet Glasgow]], baptised 26 September 1622.<ref name="Jonet1622">“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950”, database, ''FamilySearch'' (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQHV-375 : 11 February 2020), Johne Glasgow in entry for Jonet Glasgow, 1622.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-1090|George Glasgow]], baptised 4 February 1627.<ref name="George1627">“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950”, database, ''FamilySearch'' (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQHK-3WB : 16 September 2021), Johne Glasgow in entry for George Glasgow, 1627.</ref>

John's date and place of death are unknown. He died after 10 January 1613, the date of the testament that securely identifies him.

== Research Notes ==

=== Parentage ===

Two records establish the family relationship. Ninian's admission as a burgess and guild brother of Glasgow on 23 October 1596 describes him as the “second son to Robert G., fisher, burgess.” His testament, made on 10 January 1613 and confirmed on 8 May 1613, names “Johne glasgw his brother.”<ref name="Ninian" />

The current assessment accepts Robert as John's father with confidence. This is a conclusion drawn from the combined records, their shared surname and compatible chronology, rather than an explicit statement of John's parentage. The testament does not distinguish between full and half-brothers, but no concrete evidence identifies a different father. The appearance of Ninian's son Robert at the 1619 baptism also supports the proposed family reconstruction, provided the identification of John with the 1618 husband is correct.

The paternal relationship and the identification of the 1618 husband are separate questions. Confidence in Robert's parentage of Ninian's brother does not establish that brother's marriage, occupation or other proposed identities.

John's mother remains unknown. Robert's documented wife Margaret Rowand is a possible mother, but no located record explicitly identifies her as such. She should not be attached as John's mother without further evidence.

=== Birth Estimate ===

No record establishes John's date or place of birth. Glasgow is a probable birthplace because of Robert's burgess status and the family's recorded connections with the burgh, but it remains unproved.

Ninian's description as Robert's “second son” does not establish John's birth order. The only direct boundary supplied by the records securely identifying John is that he was alive by 10 January 1613.

The existing “before 1572” birth estimate depends on identifying John with the adult fisher recorded in 1572–73. If that identification is correct, he was probably born no later than the early 1550s. As the identification remains unproved, it should not be used to assign a precise birth date.

=== Identification with the Husband of Jonet Mathie ===

Ninian's brother is the leading candidate for the John Glasgow who married Jonet Mathie in 1618. The strongest supporting connection is the appearance of Ninian's proved son, [[Glasgow-1027|Robert Glasgow]], among the witnesses at the baptism of John and Jonet's son John on 13 May 1619. The other witnesses were George Glasgow and Mathew Will.<ref name="John1619" /> If the child's father was Ninian's brother, Robert was witnessing the baptism of his cousin.

This is consistent with a family connection, but is not conclusive. Neither the marriage entry nor the children's baptismal entries identifies the father's occupation, property holdings or father. The records securely identifying Ninian's brother do not give his age, occupation, residence, wife or children.

The baptismal witnesses also explain an earlier, unsupported parentage proposal. George was a proved son of a different William Glasgow, while Robert was Ninian's son. Their appearance together cannot therefore establish that George, Robert and the child's father John were brothers.

The former placement of John under [[Glasgow-3522|William Glasgow]] and [[Herbison-439|Margaret Herbesoun]] relied on that interpretation of the witnesses. Those parents are not currently attached and should not be restored as proved. Witnesses may indicate a wider kinship network, but their presence alone does not define the relationships.

=== The Glasgow Fisher Recorded in 1572–73 ===

A John Glasgow appears in Robert Glasgow's property and occupational network in the early 1570s. On 12 February 1572/73, Robert and Margaret Rowand dealt with a tenement adjoining land belonging to John Glasgow, who also witnessed the transaction. On 19 December 1573, Robert and John witnessed another transaction and were described collectively as fishers.<ref name="Protocols">Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 6, protocols 1903–1904, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc01renwgoog/page/n121/mode/2up 12 February 1572/73]; vol. 7, protocol 2002, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc00robegoog/page/n52/mode/2up 19 December 1573].</ref>

These records establish a close property and occupational association, but do not identify John as Robert's son. More than one adult John Glasgow was active in the burgh, so the fisher remains a possible identification rather than an established one.

=== Possible Mathie Family Connections ===

The proposed marriage fits an earlier association between the Glasgow and Mathie families. On 10 May 1554, David Mathy and [[Glasgow-1096|Robert Glasgow]] were fellow burgesses witnessing the same sasines.<ref name="Mathie1554">Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 1, protocols 183–184, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc07robegoog/page/n90/mode/2up 10 May 1554, printed p. 63].</ref>

David's documented son John may have been the writer later associated with the Earl of Glencairn. Tutory retours dated 20 January 1607 name Matthew, a Glasgow burgess, as the brother of the deceased John Mathie of Ibert, and list John's lawful children James, David, Agnes and Margaret.<ref name="Ibert1607">''Inquisitionum ad Capellam Domini Regis Retornatarum ... Abbreviatio'', vol. 2, tutory retours 100–101, 20 January 1607, [https://books.google.com/books?id=PiVDAAAAcAAJ digitised volume]; underlying register, National Records of Scotland, [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/browsetreeview.aspx?reference=C22 C22/3].</ref>

Jonet is not named among those four children. Suggestions that she belonged to the younger Glencairn writer's household, or was an older daughter outside the tutory proceedings, remain unproved.

If John Glasgow was Robert's son, his marriage to Jonet may have renewed the association recorded between Robert Glasgow and David Mathy in 1554. That possibility does not establish Jonet's parentage or prove the identity of her husband.

=== Disputed Child: Euphame Glasgow ===

[[Glasgow-1167|Euphame Glasgow]], baptised 30 March 1634, has been proposed as another child of John Glasgow and Jonet Mathie.<ref name="Euphame1634">“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950”, database, ''FamilySearch'' (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1Y9-V87 : 16 September 2021), Johnne Glasgow in entry for Euphame Glasgow, 1634.</ref>

The cited entry is an Edinburgh index record, despite Euphame's former inclusion in a list of High Church, Glasgow, baptisms. The same entry has also been used to place her in the otherwise coherent family of Rev. John Glassford and Jonet Morriel. It cannot establish both proposed fathers. Her identification remains unresolved pending examination of the original baptismal image.

=== Other John Glasgow Profiles ===

The following profiles must be distinguished before any merge is proposed:

* [[Glasgow-1030|John Glasgow]] is identified in the earlier analysis as the leading existing-profile match for Ninian's brother. Check whether this is the present profile before treating it as a separate merge candidate.
* [[Glasgow-1561|John Glasgow]] is chronologically possible, but no direct record connects him with Ninian's brother.
* [[Glasgow-3181|John Glasgow of Hirmanscheillis]] cannot be the brother named in Ninian's 1613 testament, because his estate had been processed by 4 May 1577. His death month reads March, but the year remains unresolved.

Name similarity and compatible dates are not sufficient grounds for merging these men. A further record linking John to an occupation, property, spouse, child or explicitly named father is needed to resolve the identity.

=== Saltcoats Sailor: Died December 1636 ===

A John Glasgow, sailor in Saltcoats within Ardrossan parish, died in December 1636. His testament dative came before Glasgow Commissary Court in April 1637. It names Isobell Gray as his widow and Katherine and Agnes Glasgow as the lawful children of the deceased. It does not expressly identify Isobell as their mother.<ref name="Saltcoats1637">National Records of Scotland, Glasgow Commissary Court, testament dative and inventory of John Glasgow, sailor in Saltcoats, NRS CC9/7/27, register pp. 478–480; original register re-read September 2026; locate by reference through the [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/search-records/legal-records/wills Scotland's People wills search].</ref>

The sailor is chronologically compatible with this profile because John's death date is unknown. However, no examined record connects Jonet Mathie's Glasgow household with Isobell Gray, Saltcoats, the sailor occupation, Katherine or Agnes. The sailor should therefore be represented separately unless a record establishes a connection through occupation, property, residence or family.<ref name="Saltcoats1637" />

John Brown or Browne appears in the estate's financial and legal dealings, but no relationship is stated. The inventory may mention an old fishing boat and equipment; that manuscript reading remains tentative.<ref name="Saltcoats1637" />

=== Unresolved Testament Index Entry: Rashlie, 1643 ===

The printed FamilySearch index lists John Glasgow “in Rashlie, parish of Kilbride,” with a date of 17 April 1643. The full-text transcript renders the place as “Rashlic.” The entry appears in ''Glasgow. Wills 1547–1800'', item #007960708, image 112, printed index p. 196, and refers to Glasgow Commissary Court register CC9/7/28.<ref name="Rashlie1643">FamilySearch, ''Glasgow. Wills 1547–1800'', item #007960708, image 112, printed index p. 196, entry for John Glasgow in Rashlie, parish of Kilbride, 17 April 1643, Glasgow Commissary Court CC9/7/28, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS8K-D98V?view=fullText&keywords=Glasgow&searchForm=advanced&lang=en&groupId=M97N-2NT index image]. This is an image of the printed index, not the underlying testament.</ref>

This is a possible match, but the index provides no age, occupation, relative or other identifying detail connecting the Rashlie resident with this profile. Other candidates noted in the existing research are [[Glasgow-1561|John Glasgow of Linlithgow]], [[Glasgow-1084|John Glasgow]], and [[Glasgow-1088|John Glasgow, baptised in Glasgow in 1619]].

The existing notes use [[Glasgow-1084|Glasgow-1084]] for both “John Glasgow of Duddingston” and “John Glasgow of Mid Calder.” Those descriptions and links need checking before they are treated as separate candidates.

The date 17 April 1643 is the indexed testament date, not an established date of death. The underlying testament must be examined before this entry can be assigned to any of these profiles.

== Biography ==

Jonet was probably born about 1597. The date is estimated from her marriage in 1618.


Jonet married [[Glasgow-1030|John Glasgow]] in Glasgow on 25 January 1618.<ref name="Marriage1618">FamilySearch, “Scotland Marriages, 1561–1910,” John Glasgow and Jonet Mathie, 25 January 1618, Glasgow, Lanark, Scotland; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYWK-WM3 permanent record].</ref>

== Research Notes ==

=== Possible Mathie–Glasgow family connection ===

The association between the surnames can be followed for more than sixty years. On 10 May 1554 David Mathy and [[Glasgow-1096|Robert Glasgow]] were fellow Glasgow burgesses witnessing the same sasines.<ref name="Mathie1554">Robert Renwick, ed., Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow, vol. 1, protocols 183–184, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc07robegoog/page/n90/mode/2up 10 May 1554, printed p. 63].</ref> David’s son John was recorded in 1571, and may be the writer recorded in 1574 and the John Mathie admitted with the Earl of Glencairn’s burgess group in 1583.<ref name="MathieJohn">Robert Renwick, ed., Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow, vol. 6, protocol 1798, 25 October 1571, printed p. 70, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc05scogoog digitised volume]; vol. 4, protocol 1036, 4 August 1574, printed p. 19, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc07scogoog digitised volume]; James R. Anderson, ed., Burgesses & Guild Brethren of Glasgow, 1573–1750, [https://electricscotland.com/history/records/scottishrecordso43scotuoft.pdf entry for 8 February 1582/83].</ref>

In 1600 Katherine Mathy, daughter of John Mathy in Clerkland, married a Glasgow maltman; John Mathie senior and junior witnessed the transaction.<ref name="Clerkland1600">Robert Renwick, ed., Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow, vol. 11, protocol 3710, [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/abstracts_of_protocols_of_the_town_clerks_of_glasgow__1900.pdf 12 November 1600].</ref> Two successive John Mathies then served the Earl of Glencairn in 1606.

Tutory retours entered on 20 January 1607 identify the deceased John Mathie of Ibert’s full brother as Matthew Mathie, burgess of Glasgow, and name John’s lawful children James, David, Agnes and Margaret.<ref name="Ibert1607">Inquisitionum ad Capellam Domini Regis Retornatarum ... Abbreviatio, vol. 2, tutory retours 100–101, 20 January 1607, [https://books.google.com/books?id=PiVDAAAAcAAJ digitised volume]; underlying register, National Records of Scotland, [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/browsetreeview.aspx?reference=C22 C22/3].</ref> The timing and Kilmaronock location make John of Ibert a strong candidate for the Glencairn servant killed in July 1606.

Jonet is not among the four children named in those tutory proceedings. She may have been older than the children requiring a tutor, but the younger Glencairn writer is presently the better candidate for her father or close kinsman. Her marriage to [[Glasgow-1030|John Glasgow]] may therefore continue the association first visible between Robert Glasgow and David Mathy in 1554.

The surname also appears as Mathei in the parish indexes. The older suggestion “Morriel” should be checked against the original marriage and baptism images.

'''⚠️ Paleographic Warning:'''

This profile is based on a testament written in 16th-century Secretary Hand. Due to the ornate and inconsistent handwriting style, all names, places, and relationships should be considered '''tentative''' and subject to '''revision''' pending further document comparison or corroboration. Interpretations are paleographically informed but speculative.

== Biography ==  
'''John Glasgow''' was born about 1590, likely in Linlithgowshire, Scotland. This estimate is based on the 1613 baptism of his daughter, [[Glasgow-3055|Jean Glasgow (bef.1613–)]]<ref>https://www.familysearch.org/tree/person/sources/MG7J-6GM</ref>.

He appears in multiple parish records as the father of children baptized in the town of Linlithgow between 1613 and 1622, suggesting he resided there for at least a decade and was part of the established Glasgow family in the area.

=== Children ===  
The following children are documented in the ''Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950'' database, all born in Linlithgow, Linlithgowshire:

* '''Jean Glasgow''' – christened 17 July 1613<ref>https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1RX-HPB</ref>  
* '''John Glasgow''' – christened 14 September 1617<ref>https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1RV-T8R</ref>  
* '''George Glasgow''' – christened 20 January 1622<ref>https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1RN-XV7</ref>  

== Research Notes ==

* The geographic setting (Linlithgowshire) and naming patterns suggest possible descent from [[Glasgow-1099|George Glasgow (abt.1580–)]] or [[Glasgow-1168|James Glasgow (abt.1540–1580)]], both associated with the greater Lanarkshire–Ayrshire–Lothian area.
* His son may have been [[Glasgow-991|James Glasgow (abt.1585–)]], also later found in Linlithgow.
* [[Glasgow-1103|Thomas Glasgow (1612–abt.1675)]], whose records also place him in the region, may be another child of John, though further documentation is needed.
* The surname in these records appears as ''Glesgow'', a common early spelling variation.


=== Parentage and generation ===
[[Glasgow-3163|Andrew Glasgow]]'s operative 1598 testament expressly names four children—Marioune, James, Andrew, and William—but does not name John.<ref>National Records of Scotland, Edinburgh Commissary Court, testament of Andrew Glasgow, CC8/8/32; printed index: [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso01scotuoft/page/n117/mode/1up ''Scottish Record Society'', p. 108].</ref> John was alive and parenting children in Linlithgow from 1613 to 1622, so this omission conflicts with treating him as Andrew's proved direct son.

The existing links to Andrew and [[Anderson-103463|Jonet Anderson]] are retained as '''uncertain working parents''', not as proved relationships. The Lothian geography could instead place John one generation lower or on a collateral line through one of Andrew's documented sons, but the evidence does not identify an exact parent. [[Glasgow-3608|John Glasgow]] is also an unproved same-name duplicate candidate; no merge is proposed.

== Sources ==

<references />

maintained_current_conclusions:
John was the father named in Linlithgow baptisms for Jean in 1613, John in 1617
and George in 1622. Those indexes do not identify his parents.

The corrected reading of Andrew Glasgow's 1597/8 testament does not support the
current Andrew/Jonet parent pair. It names Elizat Stevinsoun as Andrew's wife,
Robert as their son, and Marion, Janet and Isobel as Andrew's daughters. It does
not name this John or Jonet Anderson. Because the cited dispositive clauses need
not enumerate every child, John's omission is not by itself a direct
contradiction; the relationship is instead an unproved Lothian-cluster
hypothesis.

== Biography ==

'''John Glasgow''' is recorded as born or baptised on 18 February 1616 in Mid Calder, Midlothian, with James Glasgow and Agnes Adamson attached as his parents. The older profile cited only “Old Parish Records” for this event; the original entry and the precise birth/baptism distinction remain to be checked. The supplied NRS index names James Glasgow as father (Mid Calder OPR 694/10/28), supporting a confident father relationship for this record-defined child; the later adult-identity comparisons remain provisional.<ref>National Records of Scotland, Old Parish Registers, Mid Calder, John Glasgow, 18 February 1616, father James Glasgow, parish 694, reference 10/28; supplied Scotland’s People index, [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ repository].</ref>

A John Glasgow and [[Patoune-11|Helen Patoune]] were named as parents of [[Glasgow-3014|John Glasgow]], recorded on 11 January 1638 at Duddingston, Midlothian.<ref>Duddingston Old Parish Register, parish 684, reference FR38, “JOHNE GLASGOW/HELENE PATOUNE,” entry for Johne, 11 January 1638; citation carried from the former Glasgow-3015 profile. The original page has not been compared with this index wording.</ref>

Later entries name a John Glasgow with [[Porteous-912|Issobell Porteous]] as parents of [[Glasgow-1438|Issobell Glasgow]], recorded on 4 April 1643 in Edinburgh parish,<ref>“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” FamilySearch, [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1YN-JHD entry for Issobell Glasgow, 1643], naming John Glasgow and Issobell Porteous; cited on the child's profile.</ref> and [[Glasgow-1439|Anne Glasgow]], recorded on 20 June 1652 at Kirknewton and East Calder. The latter child's profile cites a [https://www.familysearch.org/tree/person/details/4XPK-FW2 FamilySearch tree] rather than an inspected register entry, so its details remain to be verified.

[[Glasgow-3107|James Glasgow]] is also attached as a son. His own profile documents a 1663 marriage at Polwarth but says his parentage remains unconfirmed; that attachment must not be read as an established child of this John.

== Research Notes ==

The former Glasgow-3015 profile and this profile were combined as the leading identification. The 1638 Duddingston father and the father of the 1643 and 1652 children share a name, generation and neighbouring Midlothian parishes; there is no recorded overlap in the two maternal child sequences. No death of Helen Patoune, marriage to Issobell Porteous or continuous identifier has yet been found, so identifying both fathers as one man and inferring a second union remain provisional. The earlier profile's approximate 1618 birth was an adult-status estimate, not a separate birth record.

== Biography ==
John Glasgow was christened on 13 May 1619 in the Glasgow High Kirk, Glasgow, Lanarkshire, Scotland. He was the son of [[Glasgow-1030|John Glasgow]] and [[Mathie-159|Jonet (Mathie) Glasgow]]. The witnesses recorded at his christening were [[Glasgow-1099|George Glasgow (abt.1575-abt.1640)]], Mathew Will, and [[Glasgow-1027|Robert Glasgow (abt.1583-aft.1647)]].<ref name="Baptism1619">Glasgow High Kirk Baptisms 1609-1777; Vol: 1/2957. Record for Johne Glasgow, christened 13 May 1619, lawful son of John Glasgow and Jonet Mathe. Witnesses: George Glasgow, Mathew Will, Robert Glasgow.</ref>

Sometime before 1639, John moved from his native Lanarkshire to Midlothian. He married [[Sluman-45|Margaret Sluman]], and they settled in Duddingston parish.{{citation needed }}

They had at least one known son:
* [[Glasgow-1559|John Glasgow]], christened 4 April 1639 in Duddingston, Midlothian, Scotland.<ref name="SonJohn1639">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1TP-WYX : 12 February 2020), Johne Glasgow in entry for Johne Glasgow, 1639.</ref>

The date and place of his death are unknown, but he was alive as of April 1639.

== Biography ==
Margaret Sluman's birth date and parentage are unknown. Based on the birth of her first known child in 1639, she was likely born by about 1620.

She married [[Glasgow-1088|John Glasgow]]. While their marriage record has not been found, their relationship is proven by the christening record of their son. They lived in Duddingston, Midlothian, Scotland.

Margaret and John had at least one known son:
* [[Glasgow-1559|John Glasgow]], christened on 4 April 1639 in Duddingston, Midlothian.<ref name="SonJohn1639">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1TP-WYX : 12 February 2020), Margaret Sluman in entry for Johne Glasgow, 1639.</ref>

The date and place of her death are not known, but she was alive as of April 1639.

== Research Notes ==
*   '''Top Priority:''' The primary research goal is to find a christening record for Margaret Sluman, likely born circa 1615-1623. The search should focus on the parish of Duddingston and surrounding areas in Midlothian, as this is where she was living when her son was born.
*   A search for the marriage record of Margaret and John Glasgow should be conducted in the same parishes, dated before April 1639.
*   A search should be made for other children born to the couple in the Duddingston parish registers after 1639.

** Testaments and sasines in Midlothian that mention a John/Johne Glasgow of Kirknewton or East Calder.

'''Margaret Glasgow''' was baptised at Glasgow High Kirk on 6 May 1610 as the lawful daughter of [[Glasgow-1099|George Glasgow]] and [[Stewart-65226|Margaret Steuart]]. On 18 July 1633 James, a merchant, was admitted burgess and guild brother by right of his marriage to Margaret, lawful daughter of George Glasgow, merchant, burgess and guild brother.<ref>James R. Anderson, ed., ''Burgesses & Guild Brethren of Glasgow, 1573-1750'' (Edinburgh: Scottish Record Society, 1925), p. 86, [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso43scotuoft/page/n100/mode/2up entry for James Stewart, 18 July 1633].</ref>

The structured marriage field currently gives '''7 April 1632''', while the cited OPR transcription in the earlier biography gave '''4 July 1632''' under reference 644/1 230/109. These appear to be transposed day and month values. The original OPR entry has not been checked for this update, so neither value has been silently preferred; the structured date is preserved pending inspection of the original.

The printed Glasgow testament index records “Margaret, in Byris of Kilwinning” on 8 November 1636.<ref>Francis J.
