== Biography ==

Margaret Glasgow married William Hardie, a cordiner, at Edinburgh on 16 July 1611.<ref>“Scotland, Marriages, 1561–1910,” FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYMK-1QM : accessed 11 February 2020), William Hardie and Margaret Glasgow, 1611.</ref><ref>Henry Paton, ed., ''The Register of Marriages for the Parish of Edinburgh, 1595–1700'', p. 267, [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/register_of_marriages_for_the_parish_of_edinburgh_1595-1700_~_1898.pdf#page=277 16 July 1611], naming William as a cordiner.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

No reviewed record identifies Margaret's parents or birthplace. Her structured birth before 1595 is only an uncertain adult-status estimate from the 1611 marriage.

The same published-register page records Barbara Glasgow marrying cordiner George Johnstoun in 1616 and Isobel Glasgow marrying tailor William Symountoun in 1619. This craft-marriage cluster is a useful kinship lead, not proof that the women were sisters.

=== William Hardie's identity ===
The Edinburgh marriage register lists a William Hardie, cordiner, with Eupham Wauchope on 1 September 1608, Margaret Glasgow on 16 July 1611, Catharine Leslie on 27 August 1641 and Catharine Angus on 17 November 1643.<ref>Henry Paton, ed., ''The Register of Marriages for the Parish of Edinburgh, 1595–1700'', [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/register_of_marriages_for_the_parish_of_edinburgh_1595-1700_~_1898.pdf#page=317 printed p. 307], entries under Hardie (Hardy).</ref> The repeated name and trade make these entries useful for tracing Margaret's husband, but they do not establish that all four marriages involved one man. The later entries could concern a younger namesake. Original parish and cordiner records are needed before inferring Margaret's death or additional relatives.

=== Possible family placement ===
Margaret is best placed as a possible daughter or niece of [[Glasgow-3188|Ninian Glasgow]]. Her husband William Hardie was a cordiner.<ref>Henry Paton, ed., ''The Register of Marriages for the Parish of Edinburgh, 1595-1700'', [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/register_of_marriages_for_the_parish_of_edinburgh_1595-1700_~_1898.pdf#page=277 printed p. 267], 16 July 1611.</ref> Ninian's proved son Robert was also a cordiner, while his probable son [[Glasgow-3075|William]] moved into Leith and William's son was apprenticed to a cordiner.

This direct craft and Edinburgh-Leith pattern makes Ninian's household or immediate collateral circle the leading branch, but the marriage register names no parent. The possible daughter-or-niece relationship remains uncertain.

[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==

'''Mary Glasgow''' married a man named '''Thompson''' and had children, but no record of her own birth, marriage or death has been located and her husband's forename is unknown.

She is identified by the probate citation in the estate of [[Glasgow-4070|Nancy Glasgow]] of Plattsburgh, New York. The citation, dated 14 January 1892, lists "the children of Mary Thompson whose names and places of residence are unknown" among Nancy's heirs and next of kin, in the same group as the children of John, Alexander and Robert Glasgow, of Jane (Glasgow) Dysart, of Elizabeth (Glasgow) Anderson (sons "living at Gortahar") and of Ann McClelland.<ref>''The Plattsburgh Sentinel'', 26 February 1892, p. 6 (citation dated 14 January 1892). [https://www.nyshistoricnewspapers.org/?a=d&d=plts18920226-01.1.6 newspaper page]; also printed in ''The Plattsburgh Republican'', 23 January–13 February 1892.</ref>

A New York probate citation of this period had to be directed to the testator's heirs and next of kin, so Mary was a deceased sister of Nancy — a daughter of the sibling group's father (see Research Notes).

== Research Notes ==

This is the thinnest of the sibling profiles. Mary is not named in any located Irish record; her LNAB Glasgow, her parentage and even her Irish residence are inferences from the probate citation. Her parents are reassessed as [[Glasgow-4090|John Glasgow, farmer]] (uncertain) and an unknown mother. No dates should be added without a record. A civil death of a Mary Thompson, widow of William Thompson, farmer, at Tannybrake, Connor parish, on 7 March 1888 aged 73 is an age-compatible candidate but is NOT proved to be this Mary.

== Sources ==
<references />

maintained_current_conclusions:
**Mary Thompson remains a citation-defined research subject, probably Nancy Glasgow’s sister; no household, spouse forename, birth date or birthplace is established.** Glasgow as her birth surname and John farmer as her father are inferred from the family reconstruction. No residence in County Londonderry is established for her. The live WikiTree profile has a blank birth date (API checked 29 September). The local catalogue’s estimated 1874 and estimated Derry birthplace have no record basis and are withdrawn from the current presentation; no live date or relationship change was made.

**New Scottish indexed candidate:** Mary Thomson, aged 37, married William Sneddon, aged 45, widower and collier, on **9 November 1860**, with parents **Robert Thomson** and **Mary Glasgon Thomson**. [Civil-registration bride index](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:6TLK-6T1J); [mother index](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:6TLK-6T1K). The [older marriage index](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XT1H-TBC) gives **Old Monkland, Lanarkshire**. Both indexes describe the same event. Document information: **008056939_011_M9H1-8LK, image 32**. The original image requires a FamilySearch centre or affiliate library and was not inspected. The mother is a **candidate only** for this Mary; no Irish origin, Nancy relationship or mother’s parent names have been established. Nothing is attached to this profile from that index.

The existing live biography separately mentions an **unproved Irish candidate**, a widow of William Thompson at Tannybrake, Connor, reportedly dying 7 March 1888 aged 73. No underlying source URL accompanies that claim and the original was not inspected in this review. **If those reported ages are right**, the Irish candidate would have been about eight at the Scottish daughter’s birth around 1823. That strongly opposes combining the candidates without an age correction or a different daughter identity. Robert versus William could in principle reflect remarriage, but remarriage would not fix the age problem.

A follow-up query for daughter Mary with parents Robert Thomson and Mary Glasgow returned only the 1860 marriage; no separate death was identified in the returned results. A strict query for principal Mary, spouse Robert Thomson and father surname Glasgow returned zero. These are bounded index results, not exclusions from all Scottish records. Next: establish the Old Monkland bride’s birthplace and her mother’s own death/parents; independently retrieve the Tannybrake death and reconstruct its children. Keep both candidates separate pending evidence.

== Biography ==

Marjorie Glasgow was born before 1576. She was a lawful daughter of [[Glasgow-3181|John Glasgow]] in Hirmanscheillis and Margaret Hoghame, represented on WikiTree by [[Hutcheson-1656|Margaret Hutcheson]].

John's testament dative, processed in 1577, records that Margaret Hoghame gave up his inventory on behalf of their lawful children Katherine and Marjorie Glasgow, who were appointed executors-dative.<ref name="JohnTestament">National Records of Scotland, Edinburgh Commissary Court, CC8/8/5, images 276–277, testament dative of John Glasgow in Hirmanscheillis, processed 1577; working transcription of the original manuscript.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

=== Name reading ===

The second child's forename is read from the manuscript as ''m[ar]iory'', modernised as Marjorie, following the accepted human reading of the original register (NRS CC8/8/5, images 276–277). The earlier model reading "Androw" is superseded and is not a competing current reading. Accepting the name does not by itself establish a later adult identity for this Marjorie.

=== Maternity ===

The testament calls Katherine and Marjorie John's lawful bairns and names Margaret as John's widow, but the possessive before "lauchfull barnis" is not securely distinguished as "his" or "thair", so Margaret's maternity is not securely proved and remains unproven pending direct evidence.

An earlier version associated this profile with a Margaret Glasko buried at Norwich, England, on 22 August 1588.<ref name="Norwich">"England, Deaths and Burials, 1538–1991", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:J87G-3P8), entry for Margaret Glasko, 22 August 1588.</ref> That record concerns Margaret, while the Scottish testament names this daughter Marjorie; no record connects the Norwich burial to the Hirmanscheillis family. It is therefore retained here only as an excluded same-name lead.

== Sources ==

== Biography ==

'''Marion Glasgow''' was a daughter of [[Glasgow-3163|Andrew Glasgow of uncertain Corsoun]]. Andrew's testament, made on 6 February 1597/8, provides that if his wife Elizat Stevinsoun was not pregnant, his third was to be divided among “his said sone and his said [dochter… struck through] Marione, Jonet, Isobell.”<ref name="Andrew1598">National Records of Scotland, Edinburgh Commissary Court, CC8/8/32, images 123–124, testament testamentar and inventory of Andro Glasgw, made 6 February 1597/8, death stated as 7 February, confirmed 10 July 1598; corrected working transcription of the original register images. Printed index: Scottish Record Society, ''Commissariot of Edinburgh: Register of Testaments, 1514–1600'', [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso01scotuoft/page/n117/mode/1up p. 108].</ref>

Her brother [[Glasgow-4006|Robert]] is expressly called Andrew's son by Elizat. The testament does not separately state that Elizat was this daughter's mother, so maternity should not be inferred as certain from this clause alone.<ref name="Andrew1598"/>

== Research Notes ==

=== Identity ===

Named as a lawful daughter in Andrew's 1598 testament. No later record has been securely connected to her; the same-name Glasgow women of the period have no Corsoun, Stevenson, sibling or succession bridge to this household, so none is attached here.

A separate [[Glasgow-3062|Marion Glasgow]] is identified as [[Glasgow-3188|Ninian Glasgow]]'s sister in his 1613 testament and as the mother of James Fultoun in a 1610 Glasgow baptism. Neither record names Andrew, Elizat or Corsoun. This is a same-name identity comparison, not a proved match; keep the profiles separate pending a connecting record.<ref>National Records of Scotland, Glasgow Commissary Court, CC9/7/9, images 142–145, Ninian Glasgow testament; Glasgow & West of Scotland Family History Society, [https://www.gwsfhs.org.uk/records/james-fultoun/ James Fultoun baptism index], 7 August 1610.</ref>

== Sources ==

[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]] {{Estimated Date|Birth}} == Biography == '''Robert Glasgow''' was the son of [[Glasgow-3163|Andrew Glasgow of uncertain Corsoun]] and Andrew's wife '''Elizat Stevinsoun'''. Andrew's testament, made on 6 February 1597/8, expressly describes him as:
“Robart Glasgw his sone begottin be him vpoun the said Elizat his wyff”
Andrew directed that Elizat should “bruik his [word unclear] land quhill his said Robart cum to aige,” showing that Robert had not yet attained the relevant legal majority and was intended to succeed to the land after Elizat's interim possession.National Records of Scotland, Edinburgh Commissary Court, CC8/8/32, images 123–124, testament testamentar and inventory of Andro Glasgw, made 6 February 1597/8, death stated as 7 February, confirmed 10 July 1598; corrected working transcription of the original register images. Printed index: Scottish Record Society, ''Commissariot of Edinburgh: Register of Testaments, 1514–1600'', [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso01scotuoft/page/n117/mode/1up p. 108]. The testament also names Andrew's daughters Marion, Janet and Isobel. It makes conditional provision “incais his said spous be with bairne to him”; that does not prove that an additional child was born. == Research Notes == === Identity === The profile previously represented an Andrew Glasgow created from a superseded reading of this testament; the corrected record names no such son. It has been repurposed for the directly documented son Robert. [[Glasgow-1156]], estimated born in 1582 and buried at Duddingston in 1647, is compatible by date and Lothian geography but its record names neither Andrew, Elizat, Corsoun, siblings nor the land, so it is excluded as the present match. [[Glasgow-1027]] is the proved son of Ninian Glasgow and Jonet Meik, and [[Glasgow-1096]] died before Andrew's will. Search NRS GD150/696–757, GD150/2027–2060 and GD150/320–493 for Andrew's land and an occupier succession to Robert. == Sources ==
